source.title: An Introduction to Exemplar Partitioning for Mechanistic Interpretability

record.tranche_reason: The post reports a qualitative comparison between EP regions and a canonical SAE, but does not test SAE dictionary-size scaling, nested feature families, absorption, or the effect of the SAE objective.
record.gate_note: The post's EP-versus-SAE comparison is relevant to feature correspondence but does not test any listed claim version. Other results, including AxBench scores and refusal interventions, do not measure the listed feature-splitting claims.
record.test_reason: The post introduces Exemplar Partitioning (leader-clustering into Voronoi regions) and compares it qualitatively with one canonical GemmaScope SAE. It does not vary SAE dictionary size, test parent/child absorption, compare SAE sizes or families, or test SAE objectives such as Matryoshka. The resolution sweep is over EP's threshold p, not SAE dictionary size, so no SAE splitting version is tested. The remark that the SAE 'splinters' broad EP regions into narrow features is an interpretive aside without measurement.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The author describes a small shared core between EP regions and GemmaScope SAE features and much disagreement on both sides, attributed to differing geometric commitments. More broadly, the post presents EP as a cheap, unsupervised alternative that performs similarly to SAEs in some ways (AxBench 0.881 vs SAE-A 0.911) but not others. It is not presented as a test of SAE feature splitting.
record.recipe_differences: EP uses leader-clustering of observed activations into Voronoi regions; the comparison is against a learned SAE dictionary, not a reproduction or size sweep of SAE training.
record.method_sensitivity: EP-to-SAE correspondence is described as changing with EP resolution.

fits_no_version.finding: At moderate EP resolution, roughly one in five EP regions has a strong GemmaScope SAE counterpart. Sharpening EP yields subregions the SAE lacks. The author says the SAE splinters broad EP regions into multiple narrow features, and that some SAE directions have no contiguous EP region.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Density-based exemplar partitions and sparse SAE dictionaries share only a small core of features, with disagreement attributed to different geometric commitments (density vs linear separability).

record.problems: The feature-correspondence result is qualitative apart from the approximate one-in-five figure, and the post says the experiments tested only Gemma-2-2B and the Pile. It does not test SAE size scaling.
record.rows_left_out: No other results in the post directly measure the listed SAE feature-splitting claims.

untested.parts: No SAE dictionary-size sweep; only one GemmaScope 16k SAE is used.
No test of SAE splitting across scales or SAE releases.
No test of nested SAE feature families. The EP neighbourhood example concerns EP regions only and is illustrative.
No parent/child latent absorption test. Absorption here refers to one EP region absorbing refusing prompts, which is unrelated.
No decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents.
Argues SAE and EP differ in geometric commitments, but does not test whether the sparsity objective produces splitting or compare objectives.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'discusses'/T6 classification is right. The post's 'splitting' language concerns EP resolution, which is analogous to dictionary size but is a different method, so it does not bear on the SAE versions. The AxBench, refusal, OOD, base-vs-IT drift and domain-saturation results are not about SAE feature splitting. The comments contain no relevant measurements. Only Gemma-2-2B and the Pile are used.

versions.untested_parts: No SAE dictionary-size sweep or test of smaller-to-larger SAE feature splits.
No test of the claimed SAE splitting pattern across large models or open SAE releases.
No test of nested, geometrically close SAE feature families or a representation hierarchy.
No parent-child SAE latent test for absorption or whether size or sparsity changes it.
No test of larger SAE latents decomposing into smaller SAE latents or of novel latents across SAE sizes.
The post contrasts SAE and EP geometric commitments but does not test whether the SAE objective produces splitting or whether Matryoshka SAEs change it.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Compared EP regions with canonical GemmaScope SAE features by which tokens fire each feature.
rows.measure: EP regions with a strong SAE counterpart
rows.value: roughly one in five EP regions
rows.note: This compares EP with an SAE at a stated resolution; it does not compare smaller and larger SAE dictionaries.
rows.check: Compares EP regions with a single GemmaScope SAE, roughly one in five matched. It does not measure SAE splitting with dictionary size. It is also partly a method-vs-method comparison.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Sharpened the EP resolution and compared its regions with the canonical GemmaScope SAE.
rows.measure: Correspondence of EP subregions to SAE features
rows.value: EP continues to split into subregions not carried by the SAE
rows.note: The resolution sweep is for EP, not SAE dictionary size. The post also describes disagreement in both directions: some SAE directions lack a single contiguous EP region at that resolution.
rows.check: The splitting reported is EP subregions as EP resolution sharpens, not SAE features as the dictionary grows. It is qualitative, with no value or baseline.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
